angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 356,198 km at 63.94 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.6390 +/- 0.0231 mas (same row, RUWE 1.60): 63.94 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.512 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Cointepas et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-663 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract): 356,198 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.514 +/- 0.012 solar masses from Cointepas et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-663 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3681 +/- 70 K from Cointepas et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-663 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cointepas et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-663 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-663.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.730, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-663 (pscomppars): spectral type M1 V, from Cointepas et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-663 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.07 dex, from Cointepas et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-663 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.37033, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-663 (pscomppars): rotation period 30 d, from Cointepas et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...685A..19C/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
